excerpt: Canada’s Sustainable Development Goals become meaningful when national ambitions are translated into questions that residents can examine and act on together. As a newcomer to Canada, I reflected on the relationship between the community where I reside, Silverton in southwest Calgary, Alberta, and SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).
body:
What if local climate action began not with a technology pitch, but with shared questions about affordability, access, data, place, and responsibility?

In ENVS 839, I explored how SDGs 7, 11, and 13 connect household energy, neighbourhood conditions, and climate resilience. National indicators, including energy savings, cleaner electricity, sustainable commuting, and emissions reduction, provide useful direction. Yet I found no verified Silverton-specific baseline, so responsible localization cannot mean presenting assumptions as local results.

My proposed response is a 12-week Silverton Community Energy Learning Lab with quarterly follow-ups. It would begin with a community agreement and shared rules, then use voluntary bill-reading, an energy and accessibility walk, workshops, household action pilots, resident stories, peer-facilitator development, a results forum, and community-controlled aggregate reporting. This is a learning design, not a program that has already been implemented.

The course readings challenged my engineering instinct to start with measures and solutions. Metrics remain necessary, but Two-Eyed Seeing, Ethical Space, the Four Rs, relational systems thinking, land and place, and responsibility for stories pushed me to ask who defines the problem, who controls knowledge and data, whose interpretation counts, and who benefits. As a non-Indigenous newcomer, I must engage these teachings with humility and avoid treating them as a generic management toolkit.

For professionals and community members, what evidence would convince you that a local energy initiative created meaningful influence, rather than simply good attendance?

Thank you, Elaina Guilmette, PhD, for guiding this learning.

title: Localizing the SDGs Through Community Energy
